data.title: How we build games on a 4 KB kernel
data.subtitle: What a tiny engine means when you play.
lead: Every game in the DOM VIRUS arcade runs on Fizlet, a game engine for the page whose kernel has a 4 KB gzip budget. The kernel runs the loop: read the page, step the rules, write the page back. Each game adds only the bricks it needs. Here is what that means when you play.

items.label: the Fizlet kernel, gzip (budget 4,096 B), on Fizlet 0.17.0
minor GCs in 20,000 busy steps, in each port's test

body.text: A game on Fizlet is a set of rules and a loop. Each frame the engine reads the page: where the letters and the buttons are. Then it steps the rules on typed arrays. Then it writes the page back through a ledger.
The ledger is why Recall works. Every change the game makes to the page is recorded, so the page comes back byte for byte when you are done.

blocks.heading: What you notice as a player

items: **No hitches.** A step never allocates, so the garbage collector has nothing to clean up mid-fight. Each port proves it: 20,000 busy steps, 0 minor GCs.

**Same seed, same run.** Every random roll comes from the run's seed, so a run replays exactly. That is what lets [Battlefield Blitz](/games/battlefield-blitz/) play two players in lockstep: only inputs travel, and two peers stay identical, with 0 desyncs in its tests.
**One button language.** The scoreboards share the Board UI kit, so a key in [Null Invaders](/games/null-invaders/) presses like a key in [DOM Battlefield](/games/battlefield/).
**The page comes back.** Recall restores the page byte for byte, tested in Chromium for every port.

body.text: Small is not free. Moving onto Fizlet made the games bigger in gzip bytes, by 7 to 21%. Most of that is the shared Board UI kit each game bakes in. The patch notes give every game's size, before and after.
The full story, with the size ledger game by game and what the ports taught the engine, is on fizlet.com.

items.title: Null Invaders

items.title: DOM Battlefield

items.title: Battlefield Blitz
items.body: Every tank for itself, or two players in lockstep. 40,507 B gzip (0.10.0).

items.q: How big is the Fizlet kernel?
items.a: 3,422 B gzip on Fizlet 0.17.0, as Swarm Protocol 1.4.0's size check measures it. Its budget is 4,096 B.
All six in the arcade: Null Invaders, Byte Runner, Sherman Bytes, Swarm Protocol, DOM Battlefield and Battlefield Blitz.
On fizlet.com: the kernel, the bricks and the size ledger for every port.
